name: How do I keep a room addition from looking mismatched?

mainEntity.name: How do I keep a room addition from looking mismatched with the original house?
mainEntity.text: How do I keep a room addition from looking mismatched with the original house?

acceptedAnswer.text: A room addition looks best when it feels like it was always part of the house. That usually means matching or thoughtfully complementing the roofline, siding or stucco, window shape, trim profile, and exterior proportions. Inside, the transition should preserve flow between old and new spaces so the addition does not feel like a separate box. Ceiling height, floor elevation, flooring continuity, and hallway transitions all affect how natural the project feels. In high-end Los Angeles homes, design consistency matters even more because buyers notice obvious mismatches quickly. A good architect or designer will study the existing home before drawing the addition so the new work complements the original style instead of fighting it. The best results come from planning both the structure and the aesthetics together from the start.
acceptedAnswer.description: To keep an addition from looking mismatched, match rooflines, window proportions, exterior materials, trim details, and ceiling heights as closely as possible. Good transitions inside the home also matter, because a seamless floor plan helps the addition feel original rather than appended.
